title: Rent Board Fee and Rent Increase License are easy to conflate
detail: They are separate obligations. The licence comes from Housing Inventory reporting; the fee is a per-unit annual payment (2026-2027: $59.00 per dwelling unit, due March 1). SF.gov states expressly that requesting a fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting, so an owner can be fee-paid and still unlicensed, or licensed and still owe the fee.

title: Two-unit owner-occupied exemption is conditional and unverified here
detail: AB 1482 exempts a two-unit structure only if the owner occupied one unit as a principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU. Whether the owner ever occupied a unit in this building was not supplied, so no exemption is asserted.

title: In-law or second structure on the lot changes coverage
detail: SF.gov states that a single-family dwelling with a LEGAL in-law unit is a two-unit building and is not exempt, that with an ILLEGAL in-law unit it is also a two-unit building and is not exempt UNLESS both units are rented together as a single tenancy, and that a single-family dwelling is not exempt if another residential structure is on the same lot. The owner described two units, which is consistent with Rent Ordinance coverage, but the official lot and building record was not supplied. Wording of this detail corrected 2026-11-08 - see F36.

title: Pending legislation could affect banked and capital-improvement increases
detail: On November 9, 2026 the Rent Board posted a notice about Board File 261020. The proposal would temporarily limit combined banked and capital-improvement increases to 10% per year; if enacted as currently proposed, it would apply to banked increases noticed on or after September 15, 2026 and capital-improvement increases based on petitions filed on or after that date. Legistar showed Pending Committee Action and no enactment on November 10, and the record was re-opened on November 13, 2026 with the same result: still Pending Committee Action, no final action, no enactment date and no enactment number (newest history row 10/7/2026 Youth Commission response; a sixth attachment 'Comment Ltrs' is now listed). This is not current law and may change. A 90-day notice does not establish that an increase is lawful. Check the status again immediately before serving any banked or capital-improvement notice; its effect on either unit is unverified.

title: The proposed-cap notice, the Legistar record and the draft ordinance do not fully align on retroactivity or on how the 10% is measured
detail: Verified 2026-11-10 from two official pages and re-verified 2026-11-11 against the Legistar attachment Leg Ver1. (1) Retroactivity: the November 9, 2026 notice says the proposal would apply to banked increases noticed on or after September 15, 2026, a date earlier than the notice and earlier than any possible enactment; the ordinance was introduced 9/15/2026. Neither page says whether an increase noticed between 9/15/2026 and enactment would be caught. (2) Duration: the notice calls the measure temporary; the Legistar title says three years; the draft text makes the limit effective through December 31, 2029 and lets landlords accumulate the excess and impose it on or after January 1, 2030. (3) Measurement: the draft adds proposed Sec. 37.3(h), which limits combined banked and capital-improvement increases to 10% of the lowest base rent in effect at any time in the 12 months before the increase takes effect, and does not state how it interacts with the separate annual allowable increase under Sec. 37.3(a)(1). The draft is NOT enacted: the Legistar status remains Pending Committee Action.

title: 94122 SAFMR is not a market rent, a cap, or a comparison for these units
detail: The published FY2026 and FY2027 SAFMRs are HUD 40th-percentile gross-rent benchmarks used for voucher payment standards. They are not a market-rent appraisal, not a lawful rent ceiling, and not a basis for any increase. Comparing them with the case contract rents would require each unit's bedroom count and utility treatment, which are not published, so no comparison, percentage or market-rent conclusion is stated. Bedroom counts stay blank.

title: "Law passed in 2023" - the local small-building operative date, not a state statute
detail: The reporting and Rent Increase License duty is a San Francisco ordinance (Administrative Code Ch. 37, Sec. 37.15, added by Ord. No. 265-20, effective January 18, 2021), not a California state law. The date 2023 comes from the LOCAL operative date for condominiums and buildings with 1-9 residential units (March 1, 2023, per Sec. 37.15(c) and Rent Board Rule 13.14); buildings with 10 or more units began reporting July 1, 2022. The actual 2023 state law, SB 567 (Chapter 290, Statutes of 2023), amended the statewide Tenant Protection Act (just cause and the state rent cap) and became operative April 1, 2024; no provision of that bill requires an owner to report a rent increase to a local rent board. This flag records the distinction so the licence duty is not attributed to state law, and so the 2023 date is not mistaken for the year the ordinance was enacted. Verified against the primary texts on 2026-11-13.

title: Whether Civil Code 1947.7 reaches the SF licensing scheme is unresolved
detail: Civil Code 1947.7(b) limits penalties and remedies for an owner in substantial compliance with an ordinance that controls rents and 'requires the registration of rents', and 1947.7(c) restores denied annual adjustments prospectively - the state backstop an owner would naturally look for. But SF Administrative Code Sec. 37.15(d) states that the Rent Board 'shall not operate a rental registry within the meaning of California Civil Code Sections 1947.7 - 1947.8', which cuts against the shield applying here, and no San Francisco official page applies it to the Rent Increase License rule. The site therefore publishes the question blank (Q-25) and never argues section 1947.7 as a defense. Section 1947.7 was read directly from leginfo on 2026-11-13 (S93); a landlord-tenant attorney, not this site, should answer the applicability question.
